html:
Kazi Nazrul Islam was a Bengali poet, songwriter and musician, born in 1899 at Churulia in West Bengal, who became the national poet of Bangladesh and is buried in Dhaka.

He served in the British Indian Army in the First World War and became famous in 1922 with Bidrohi, the Rebel, a fierce poem of defiance. The British jailed him for his writing against colonial rule. He wrote against religious hatred and for the equality of women and the poor, and used both Hindu and Muslim themes. He composed nearly 3,000 songs, known as Nazrul Geeti.

In 1942 an illness left him unable to speak or write. In 1972 the new government of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman brought him to Dhaka, where he died in 1976. His marching song Chal Chal Chal is the national march, and with Tagore he is the voice of the Bengali culture defended in the Language Movement.
sum: Kazi Nazrul Islam was a Bengali poet, songwriter and musician, born in 1899 at Churulia in West Bengal, who became the national poet of Bangladesh and is buried in Dhaka.
